prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant boundary: River Intake Pump Station (Ironwood)/Raw Water Screen Channel–High Service Pump Header; distribution excluded. Intake requires demand/depth/equipment/downstream permissives; faults/local-control inhibit; lost permissives alarm/stop. Screen sends Rake Torque Snapshot; high-high needs field confirmation. Chief Operator authorizes Storm Intake Mode/urgent-dose corrections, confirms recovery, reviews next-day capacity/quality/demand before maintenance release. Coagulant Dosing Skid (Marigold) sends Alum Batch Ticket; Laboratory Technician verifies lot. Incremental verified-feedback dosing; feedback loss: last-safe/approved-fixed dose plus grabs. Duty Engineer approves temporary adjustments/configuration/forecasts, reviews discrepancies/work constraints, may defer nonessential maintenance. North Filter Gallery (Cobalt)/South Filter Gallery receive advisories; South sends Filter Run Exception Note. Backwash considers duration/headloss/turbidity/upstream; return requires compliant rinse/stability; maintenance preserves demand/wash capacity. Overrides require justification/monitoring/restoration. Chlorine Contact Basin: Chlorine Residual Alarm requires assessment/independent grabs. Clearwell Level Controller changes coordinate with High Service Pump Header plan. Backwash Recovery Tank returns require consequential-event sampling. Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (Sparrow) receives custody-controlled samples from six locations, verifies acceptance conditions, sends checked Jar Test Photograph Set. Laboratory Technician sends Sample Chain Slip; records discrepancies; preserves custody for Chief Operator/Duty Engineer/regulatory auditors. Late/temperature-compromised results: troubleshooting-only; failed quality checks require investigation/documented correction-or-rejection. Field readings provisional pending matched laboratory comparison; contradictions notify Chief Operator; storm sampling continues until stability. SCADA Historian Server (Lantern) retains operating records/shared timestamps. Maintenance Planner (Quarry) checks work-order equipment/isolations/parts/closure evidence and snapshot/rake loading. Orders require approved window/responsible-person/return-condition. Lockout covers electrical/hydraulic/pneumatic/chemical/stored-energy hazards; craft verifies locally, operations acknowledges before intervention; Ironwood needs tags/verification/turnover acknowledgment. Handover covers isolations/limits/unavailability/abnormalities. Chemical Supplier Driver sends Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log before unloading; approved routes/areas/operator-observed access; coagulant-transfer hose/containment/washdown inspection; chlorine-work ventilation/gas-monitoring/communications. Residuals Hauler removes material. Distribution Dispatcher receives restrictions and advance maintenance notice affecting header/North

New part:
S118: When Storm Intake Mode is active, discretionary work is reviewed again because debris loading, chemical demand, and operator workload may change quickly.
S119: A Chlorine Residual Alarm during maintenance causes the affected task to pause until operations confirms whether the alarm is process-related or maintenance-induced.
S120: The Laboratory Technician supports work control by confirming sampling needs and by reporting any acceptance concern that could delay equipment return.
S121: The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench remains available for maintenance-related samples when water quality confirmation is required before a unit is returned to service.
S122: Evidence for return to service may include local inspection results, functional test readings, instrument response checks, sample results, and operator acceptance comments.
S123: Equipment is returned to service only after temporary jumpers, bypasses, tools, spare parts, and barriers have been removed or formally accepted for continued use.
S124: If a post-maintenance test fails, the work order stays open and the Chief Operator determines whether the equipment remains isolated or can be operated under restriction.
S125: The SCADA Historian Server retains operating data needed to compare pre-work and post-work performance for pumps, dosing systems, filters, and level controls.
S126: Following maintenance closeout, disinfection control is returned to normal service only after the Chief Operator confirms that the chlorine feed controls, residual instruments, and level indications are responding consistently in the SCADA Historian Server.
S127: The Chlorine Contact Basin is operated to maintain the required contact time under the current production rate, basin level, and measured disinfectant residual.
S128: Operators adjust chlorine feed gradually so that changes in residual do not outrun mixing and contact time through the Chlorine Contact Basin.
S129: When a Chlorine Residual Alarm occurs, the control room verifies analyzer sample flow, compares the reading with a grab sample result, and holds any planned production increase until the condition is understood.
S130: The Laboratory Technician provides confirmatory residual results when analyzer drift, sample line fouling, or an unexpected residual trend is suspected.
S131: The Clearwell Level Controller maintains normal storage within established operating limits that protect disinfectant contact, reserve volume, and high-service pump suction conditions.
S132: Low clearwell level interlocks are configured to prevent pump operation from drawing the storage volume below the minimum level needed for safe hydraulic operation.
S133: High clearwell level alarms give operators time to reduce production or adjust downstream pumping before overflow conditions develop.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
